reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it provides an operational tutorial for adding BNB Smart Chain and BUSD BEP20 tokens in Trust Wallet and opening a BNB receiving address. Although the title refers to creating a Forsage account and the speaker mentions receiving dollars from another person, the supplied content does not show a deceptive promise, sensitive-credential request, recruitment structure, or payment-for-earnings flow.

citations.quote: First of all, click on 3 lines above. From here turn off all 3 tokens, 1st, 2nd and 3rd And turn on the 4th number BNB Smart Chain
In the search box for BUSD, so there are quite a lot of BUSD tokens, from which you have to put BUSD BP20
And after that you have to copy Receiving address And you can easily receive your dollars on wazzapp if you want to buy with any person

opening.argument: The video links a concrete wallet action to obtaining money: viewers are told to add BNB Smart Chain and BUSD, copy a receiving address, and then are told they can “easily receive” dollars through WhatsApp. That is more than neutral wallet literacy because the requested setup is presented as the route to an easy asset-receipt outcome. The title also frames the setup as a way to create a Forsage account, tying the wallet configuration to participation in a named program. A careful judge can therefore treat the tutorial as a low-barrier acquisition pitch, even though the promised dollars are described through a person-to-person purchase rather than a formal payout.

citations.quote: How to add BUSD & BNB Token in Trust Wallet to create Forsage Account
after that you have to copy Receiving address
you can easily receive your dollars on wazzapp if you want to buy with any person

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the steps operational does not answer the money-linked instruction. The video does not merely explain what tokens are; it directs viewers to configure them, copy a receiving address, and connects that action to easily receiving dollars. The absence of an explicit guarantee or credential request does not remove the solicitation-like pathway created by the wallet setup and external messaging reference.

citations.quote: these both tokens will be added to your trust wallet
you can easily receive your dollars on wazzapp

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The quoted steps establish wallet configuration and address copying, but they do not establish that viewers receive a free reward or unusually easy payout for performing those steps. The dollar reference is conditional on buying from another person, and the material does not identify a payout, claim process, or guaranteed return. Creating a Forsage account also does not itself show an acquisition promise.

citations.quote: if you want to buy with any person
to create Forsage Account

opening.argument: Several genuine risk signals appear together: crypto wallet configuration, BUSD and BNB tokens, a receiving-address workflow, an external WhatsApp contact, and language describing dollars as easy to receive. The screen sequence visibly ends at a BNB receiving screen with copy and share controls, while the narration directs viewers to copy that address. In combination, these signals make the content functionally closer to an easy-access money opportunity than a self-contained educational demonstration. The lack of a detailed explanation of counterparties or transaction safeguards strengthens the concern, because viewers are encouraged toward an external money flow without the video establishing who is trustworthy or what they will receive.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense isolates each signal as ordinary wallet use, but the relevant issue is their combination. The video pairs token activation with an address for receiving funds and an external WhatsApp pathway, then characterizes receipt as easy. A generic tutorial label does not explain why the content culminates in a money-receipt workflow or why viewers are directed toward an outside contact.

citations.quote: in your backend, these both tokens will be added to your trust wallet
you can easily receive your dollars on wazzapp

true_side_reply.rebuttal: These are risk indicators, not proof of a scam promise. A receiving address is a normal wallet feature, and the frame shows the wallet’s receive interface rather than a reward or claim screen. The narration describes buying from another person, not receiving free money for completing the tutorial. No supplied evidence shows deception, a guaranteed outcome, or a required payment to unlock funds.

citations.quote: if you want to buy with any person

opening.argument: Although presented as technical instruction, the content can be read as promotional guidance for joining and funding a Forsage-related activity. The title does not simply say how to use Trust Wallet; it expressly presents token setup as the means to create a Forsage account. The description supplies a WhatsApp number for technical knowledge, and the narration directs viewers to prepare the wallet and copy a receiving address before discussing easy dollar receipt. That combination steers viewers from setup to participation and outside contact, so the tutorial framing should not prevent the judge from recognizing a solicitation for an easy asset-acquisition pathway.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The title and description are not incidental: they identify the account purpose and provide a contact route, while the narration supplies the exact wallet actions needed to proceed. Describing those actions as education does not eliminate their promotional effect. The viewer is being moved toward an account, a receiving address, and an external transaction relationship, not merely shown abstract software features.
